topic_title: Wrong Product Due to Missing Alpha Hydrogen

notes_list.title: Check Alpha-H Before Aldol
notes_list.basic_overview: Before predicting an aldol reaction, determine whether the carbonyl compound has at least one alpha-hydrogen capable of enolate formation.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
If a carbonyl compound lacks alpha-H, ordinary self-aldol chemistry is not available. Benzaldehyde is the classic example. Under strong base it can instead undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Before predicting an aldol reaction, determine whether the carbonyl compound has at least one alpha-hydrogen capable of enolate formation. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
